clue.text: Host withdraws an employee from the creamery

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull back, so the word for host is read backwards

blocks.note: a host is a great number, a myriad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party host walks out on a worker at the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: MYRIAD backwards is DAIRYM; AN is added to make DAIRYMAN. 'Host' looks like a person but means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairyman is a worker employed in a dairy, the place where milk is turned into cream and butter.

clue.text: Himalayan native called toward peak after dropping one

indicators.note: dropping one means the letter standing for one, the Roman numeral, is removed
in a down entry, heading toward the peak means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to call someone over the airwaves is to radio them
the Roman numeral for one, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A mountain local shouted up toward the summit, having lost a member of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: RADIOED without its I is RADOED; read upwards in this down light it becomes DEODAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a cedar tree that grows natively in the western Himalayas.

clue.text: Due to receive male rat

blocks.note: to be in for something is to be due to receive it
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be given a male rat, perhaps as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is the verb: to rat on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is slang for telling tales to the authorities, which is to inform on someone.

clue.text: I'm formally going, out of misguided courtesy etc, past bank

indicators.note: out of here means the letters of etc are taken away from the longer word
misguided letters have been sent the wrong way, so what remains is rearranged

blocks.note: these three letters are removed
taken as written before the removal
since can mean ago or in the past
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a gathering out of mistaken politeness, walking past a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: COURTESY minus C, E and T leaves OURSY, rearranged to YOURS; SINCE plus RELY completes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the formal sign-off of a letter, the writer's way of taking leave at the end.

clue.text: Highly-thought-of base fills with gas

indicators.note: something that fills goes inside, so the base letter is placed within the other word

blocks.note: A-rated, given the top rating
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A well-regarded military base is pumped full of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes after the first A of A-RATED. 'Fills' looks like part of the definition, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerated drinks have had gas forced into them, so they come carbonated, fizzing with gas.

clue.text: European city felt harsh winds

indicators.note: something that winds back on itself turns around, so the phrase is read from the end

blocks.note: to feel cold is, loosely, to be cold
raw weather is harsh

explanation.surface: A traveller found a city bitterly cold in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like the noun after harsh, but it is a verb telling you to turn the whole phrase round.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, a city in central Europe.

clue.text: Multiplied by x on occasion

blocks.note: first meaning: x stands for some number
second meaning: several ..., now and then

explanation.walkthrough: The algebra reading is literal: multiplying by x means taking something x times. The everyday reading means 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in maths, the phrase describes multiplication by an unknown; in speech it means several occasions.

clue.text: In it, you finally note the tan?

indicators.note: in places the following letters inside the word for it
finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
the closing letter of you
NB, nota bene, means note well
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lying out in it, you finally notice your tan.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'it' often means sex appeal. 'Tan' is the verb here, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan is to lie out in sunshine to darken the skin, the verb also meaning to sunbathe.

clue.text: Hold crutches close to face in hospital-room fray

indicators.note: in places the closing letter inside the word for a hospital room
in a down entry, what crutches something supports it from underneath, so it goes below
'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'face'

blocks.note: a ward is a room of hospital beds
the final letter of face
to own is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: A patient on crutches tries to stay calm amid a scuffle on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crutches' looks like walking aids, but in a down light it says one piece props the other up from below.
explanation.definitionFit: To fray is to wear thin through rubbing, eroding gradually, as a cuff wears down.

clue.text: Taken unawares by fraud at work, grand swiped

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being moved about into a new order
swiped means taken, so the abbreviation for grand is taken into the letters being rearranged

blocks.note: as in a play of Shakespeare's, by him
taken as written for rearranging
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A firm is caught out by a fraudster who has swiped a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiped' says the G is taken into the mix with FRAUD before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught off guard is to be surprised while unprepared, which is what being taken unawares means.

clue.text: CV updated with this ingredient for coq au vin?

indicators.note: updated means reworked into a new version, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the dish whose letters are the full set
these two letters are taken out of the dish's letters, leaving those of the answer

explanation.surface: A cook asks what ingredient goes into coq au vin, while updating a CV.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: CV plus the answer, rearranged, makes COQ AU VIN. So remove C and V from the dish and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinoa is a grain-like seed used as a cooking ingredient, though it does not belong in a French chicken stew.

clue.text: Ace admitted to the same hearing? No

indicators.note: the same, followed by hearing, says two words are identical to the ear, sounding alike

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent, ace

explanation.surface: A top player is let into the same court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The slang word def, meaning brilliant, is said exactly like the answer. 'Hearing? No' is the definition: no hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deaf has no hearing, so 'hearing? No' describes the condition by its absence.

clue.text: General dealing with company's administrators

blocks.note: first meaning: applying to everyone, universal
second meaning, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military officer, but it is the adjective; the second half reads the phrase literally as covering a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: An across-the-board measure is a general one, applying equally to all; a company's board is its body of directors.

clue.text: See 12
Was exploiting chief at the Washington Post?

blocks.note: the paper is American, so US
ED, the editor, is a newspaper's chief

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the newspaper's boss was taking advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: A US ED is the editor at an American paper such as the Washington Post.
explanation.definitionFit: To use someone is to exploit them; the past tense matches 'was exploiting' closely enough.

clue.text: See 3
The way to follow pro ultimately remains to be seen

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
the final letter of remains
how is the way something is done

explanation.surface: How a professional's career finishes is yet to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow' places the way at the end, after pro and the last letter of remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for show is done for appearance's sake, to be seen by others rather than to be useful.

clue.text: Noblewoman is confined within tent, exit barred

indicators.note: exit is abbreviated to a single letter, and barred means it is kept out
confined within means held inside, so the two letters go into the tent

blocks.note: a marquee is a large tent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is trapped in a marquee with the way out blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual abbreviation for exit; only one of the tent's two Es is barred.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquise is the wife of a marquis, or a woman holding that rank of nobility in her own right.

clue.text: On the way out of Nod, all told

definitions.text: On the way out of Nod

blocks.clueFragment: On the way out of Nod
blocks.note: first meaning: waking up, leaving the land of Nod, which is sleep
second meaning: amounting to, in total

explanation.walkthrough: The land of Nod is a jokey name for sleep, from the Bible's land east of Eden. The comma splits the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to means regaining consciousness, and a bill coming to ten pounds totals that, all told.

clue.text: Going forward from rear secured RAF officer's admiration at the outset

indicators.note: from the rear means starting at the back, so everything is read backwards
the outset is the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to win something is to secure it
FO is a Flying Officer in the Royal Air Force
the possessive letter taken as written
the first letter of admiration

explanation.surface: From behind, a pilot officer won the early admiration of his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: WON, FO, S and A are strung together and then read backwards. 'Going forward' tempts you to read forwards, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going forward is business jargon for from this point on, which is what 'as of now' means.

clue.text: With surfing facilitator it lacks substance

blocks.note: W is short for with
an ISP, internet service provider, makes web surfing possible

explanation.surface: A computer help desk is useless even with an internet provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfing' is browsing the web, not riding waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a thin, flimsy strand of smoke or hair, something with almost no body or substance.

clue.text: Ideal facility in back of digestive factory!

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow
back means read in the opposite direction, from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A biscuit factory boasts of an ideal canteen at the back of the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A digestive is a plain British biscuit, so the surface pictures a biscuit works. Reading digestivE FACtory backwards finds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a place to eat, and one at a biscuit factory would be an ideal amenity for staff.

clue.text: A Knight lost, a man pinned by one Black Queen?

indicators.note: the letters for a and knight are lost, removed from the words that follow
something pinned by another is held in place inside it

blocks.note: Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer and TV presenter
A plus N, the chess abbreviation for knight; these are removed
taken as written before the removal

explanation.surface: In a chess game, Black loses a knight and has a piece pinned by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is a decoy: Black is Cilla Black, a British pop singer and TV host, and N is the chess abbreviation for knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Camilla became Queen consort when King Charles III acceded to the British throne in 2022.

clue.text: Work round the ticket with a northern traveller

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: a machine that works is one that goes
the ticket means just the thing, it
taken as written
N is short for northern

explanation.surface: A northern traveller sorts out a train ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ticket' is an old idiom for exactly the right thing, as in 'that's the ticket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gitano is a Spanish Romani person, one of a traditionally travelling people.

clue.text: I'm with you on historical tours

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the second word goes around the first

blocks.note: something historical is old, aged
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone joins a friend on a series of heritage tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'agreed' tells someone you share their view, the same as saying you are with them.

clue.text: Misquoting the Bible? Just its last, staggering, revelation!

indicators.note: just its last means only the final letter of the book is taken
staggering means lurching unsteadily, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging
the final letter of Bible

explanation.surface: Someone misquotes Scripture, and the last book, Revelation, is a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misquoting' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged; 'staggering' is the real signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite something is an exclamation for anything remarkable, and a revelation is a surprising, eye-opening thing.

clue.text: See 24
See 6
Classical painter right to make an entrance? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, with its last letter cut off

blocks.note: ingress is the right of entry

explanation.surface: A painter asks if he has the right to make a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: INGRESS loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Meat Loaf entertains party in Maine?

indicators.note: to entertain is to take someone in as a guest, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a cake can be a loaf-shaped block, as in a cake of soap or a loaf cake
lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: The rock singer Meat Loaf plays host to a party on the Maine coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat Loaf was an American rock singer; the name must be split into two separate words to parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is a New England beach party where clams and other seafood are cooked, typical of Maine.

clue.text: Could this be Jane Eyre writer's emphatic refusal to retire?

indicators.note: to retire is to fall back, so the words are read from the end

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me, so writer's is my
nope is an emphatic no

explanation.surface: Charlotte Bronte flatly refuses to retire from writing.
explanation.walkthrough: MY NOPE is read backwards. 'Writer's' looks like Charlotte Bronte's, but in crosswords it is the setter's own: my.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is the character who gives her name to the novel, which makes her its eponym.

clue.text: Key item old man takes on the piste?

blocks.note: PA is dad, and the item is his, so PA'S
a fencing piste is the strip where bouts are fought with swords

explanation.surface: A father wonders what essential kit to take skiing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piste' suggests skiing, but it is also the fencing strip; what an old man takes onto it is PA'S SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is the secret word that unlocks access to an account, functioning as its key.
